transcript:
Header:
Date: 2026-04-06
Time: 15:00 PT
Duration: 52 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Kim (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (Redwood CSM), Mary Lopez (Aurora CTO), Ethan Chu (Aurora Dir ML), Sana Patel (Aurora PM), Alex Rivera (Infra)

Auto-summary (auto-gen): Walkthrough of Redwood Console focusing on usage analytics and per-route cost breakdown. Customer asked about data residency, retention, and dedicated capacity options. Next steps captured.

Transcript:
[00:00] Jordan: Hey everyone thanks for joining, um we'll get started — I'm Jordan Kim from Redwood, this is Priya our solutions engineer and Marcus our CSM, um thanks for taking the time. Mary, Ethan, Sana, Alex, you all good to start?
[00:08] Mary: Yep good to go, thanks Jordan.
[00:10] Ethan: Yeah thanks, excited to see the console walkthrough.
[00:15] Priya: Great — quick agenda, I'll demo the usage analytics, then per-route dashboards and cost breakdowns, show how to filter by model/route and time windows, and then we'll talk about retention, audit logs and dedicated options.
[00:26] Sana: Sounds good — high level we're evaluating Redwood for our customer support assistant, need visibility into per-route cost and latency, and want to understand how to isolate PII in logs.
[00:36] Jordan: Perfect, that'll be the framing. Priya over to you.

[02:05] Priya: (screen share) Okay jumping into the console, this is the Usage Analytics page. On the top we show aggregated tokens, requests, and cost burn over selectable windows. You can group by model, route, team, or region. For Aurora, you can set per-route budgets and alerts so that if a route is burning more than expected you get notified or traffic can be throttled.
[02:40] Alex: Quick q — is the cost number actual billed amount or an estimate?
[02:44] Priya: It's an estimate derived from the unit economics we show — per-token compute + storage factors — we align it to your billing cycle. For Dedicated customers we can map to capacity commits and show amortized GPU cost as a separate view.
[03:05] Ethan: Can you show per-route SLOs? We need to ensure sub-200ms tail latency for our low-latency path.
[03:11] Priya: Yep, go to the per-route dashboard — here I select the 'low-latency-support' route. You see throughput, p50/p95/p99 latencies, token distribution, and an estimated cost per request. There's a little caveat that very bursty patterns skew per-request estimates because of batching, KV-cache hits, etc — we surface KV "cache" hit rates (sometimes transcribed as KV cash) and batching factors to explain discrepancies.
[03:50] Mary: Are the latency histograms correlated with model variants? Like if we fallback to a smaller quantized variant does the dashboard show that?
[03:58] Priya: Yes — model variants are first-class here. You can split by model version, quantization profile, or hardware tier. We also show rollouts and can overlay canary vs baseline so you can see difference in cost and latency in real time.

[06:10] Jordan: One common ask is how to attribute cost to product teams — Priya, walk through per-route cost allocation.
[06:18] Priya: Sure — per-route cost breakdown lives on the Cost tab. For each route we break out token compute cost, infra share (amortized GPU), storage/embeddings ops, and caching savings. You can also export a CSV to feed back into your internal chargeback system. Here I'm selecting a 30-day window and grouping by team tag — notice the top three routes account for 72% of spend and you can click into any route to see sample requests and prompt/response size distribution.
[07:02] Sana: Nice — is there a way to hide raw prompts in the export? We can't export PII.
[07:08] Priya: Yes — redaction and retention controls are configurable. By default for Hosted we store minimal logs, and you can enable PII redaction, automatic prompt truncation, or send only aggregates. For Private / VPC deployments you can disable transcript retention entirely and use local log sinks.
[07:28] Alex: On the security front we need audit logs and SSO. What's the retention and searchability for audit trails?
[07:34] Marcus: We provide audit logs with configurable retention; logs are searchable in the console and can be exported to your SIEM. For SOC2 customers we keep an immutable audit trail and integrate with customer KMS for key rotation. We'll share the security packet after this call.

[09:00] Ethan: Can we run a bench to measure per-route unit cost using our traffic? We'll want to compare hosted vs Dedicated amortized numbers.
[09:07] Jordan: Absolutely — our recommended POC is a two-week bench where we replay a sampling of your traffic and measure p95 latency, throughput, and per-token cost. We can also run a Dedicated capacity estimate to show amortized cost if you commit X GPUs.
[09:25] Priya: I'll add that we can simulate batching effects — if your workload can tolerate higher latency we show how batching reduces token cost by up to 40% in some profiles; that's surfaced in the Optimize tab with recommended batching/quantization profiles.

[11:40] Mary: A question on multi-region — we have EU customers and need data residency. Can we pin routes to regions?
[11:47] Priya: Yes you can route by policy — per-route region affinity is supported. We also show region cost differentials in the console. For Private deployments we support on-prem nodes in your EU subnet.

[13:20] Alex: About per-route throttling — if a route goes rogue can we limit it automatically?
[13:25] Priya: Yes, the console allows per-route quotas and burst policies. You can set a hard cap and a soft-alert threshold; additionally there's automated fallback to cheaper model variants if latency SLOs are still met.

[15:05] Ethan: You mentioned KV hit rates earlier — can we get details at the request level? Like which requests hit the prefix cache versus miss?
[15:14] Priya: We surface KV cache hit rates aggregated per-route and you can sample request traces to see cache behavior. Full traces are optional because of privacy. Sampling rate is configurable.

[17:50] Jordan: Let's hop into a quick demo of the CSV export and the per-route chargeback UI. Priya: (clicks) export-ready CSV, it's got route, team tag, tokens_in, tokens_out, compute_cost_est, infra_amortized, total_cost. Note: compute_cost_est is model-dependent and we include a model catalog mapping to unit costs.
[18:28] Sana: Will the export align to our internal FY accounting? We typically break down by feature team and product line.
[18:34] Priya: Yep you can map Redwood route tags to your team ids and export with custom columns — we support a mapping table in the console and saved exports.

[20:00] Mary: About support SLAs — if we go Dedicated can we have a guaranteed p99?
[20:05] Marcus: We offer SLA-backed latency targets for Dedicated customers with committed capacity and playbooks for escalations. The exact p99 guarantee depends on traffic shape and commit level, but we'll model it during the procurement phase.

[22:40] Ethan: There's often a mismatch between theoretical per-token cost and what we see in practice due to pre and post processing. How do you account for that?
[22:48] Priya: Good question — console lets you annotate requests with upstream processing cost and we encourage tagging of pre/post tokens. The cost breakdown will show upstream pre/post overheads separately.

[25:10] Alex: One more infra question — does the console surface GPU utilization and slot allocation? We want to plan capacity.
[25:17] Priya: Yes on the Dedicated view you can see GPU utilization, average batch sizes, and queue lengths per machine pool. That view helps you size pools and shows opportunities to reduce cost by changing pooling policies.

[28:00] (discussion about sample dashboard links, Priya shares link in chat)
[30:12] Priya: I'm posting the per-route sample dashboard link and the example CSV to the meeting chat — you'll have access to the demo tenant view for 7 days.

[31:40] Mary: Great, couple of asks — 1) send the per-route cost spreadsheet, 2) show a mapping of our top ten routes with projected monthly cost, 3) security docs (SOC2) and network architecture for Private option.
[31:55] Jordan: Noted, we'll deliver those.

[34:00] Sana: For the POC, can you replay 5% of our traffic or do you need more? We can sample at the edge.
[34:07] Priya: 5% is usually sufficient to validate latency and cost behavior, but we'll discuss sample size in the kickoff. Also we'll need a 1-2 day window to ingest sample CSVs and spin up the bench environment.

[36:20] Ethan: Any gotchas we should be aware of — like cold KV cache effects?
[36:25] Priya: Cold cache and cold-starts matter for short runs; that's why we recommend a warm-up period during the bench and we expose cache warm-up metrics in the console. Quantization can also affect output quality; we include eval hooks to compare outputs across variants.

[39:00] Marcus: We'll also include a template eval set so you can track regression tied to changes in batching/quantization.

[41:10] Mary: Ok this is helpful. Can we get an itemized estimate for both hosted and Dedicated for 10M tokens/mo?
[41:18] Jordan: Yes Jordan: we'll send an itemized sheet that shows hosted per-token estimate and amortized Dedicated costs for commit levels (2x A100 equivalents, 4x, etc).

[43:50] (brief cross-talk about scheduling)
[45:00] Priya: Quick note on console retention: default logs 30 days for hosted demo tenants, configurable up to your policy for enterprise customers. For Private we hand over control to your logging stack.

[47:30] Alex: Good — we also need KMS integration for encryption at rest.
[47:34] Marcus: We support customer-managed KMS in Private and Dedicated with HSM-backed keys for compliance packages.

[49:10] Jordan: Alright let's recap — action items: Jordan send pricing + per-route cost spreadsheet, Priya share demo recording and links, Ethan provide sample traffic, Marcus share security packet. We'll aim to schedule POC kickoff for the week of 2026-04-20. Any other questions?
[49:28] Mary: No, that covers it, thanks everyone.
[49:34] Ethan: Thanks, appreciate it.
[49:36] Priya: Thanks all, recording and links in chat.
[49:40] (meeting ends)

Notes on transcript quality: Some transcription artifacts present — e.g., "KV cash" instead of KV cache, occasional misattribution of short interjections.
